summary: ACCEPT. Records refusal_origin and refusal_code on the trade intent, closing the W2 provenance gap I traced: the system already distinguished a client abort from a broker rejection in the LOGS and in the fan-out outcome path (WHLR carried outcome=rejected_client_abort) while trade_intents.status read plain 'rejected' -- so the distinction existed everywhere EXCEPT the one surface every count is derived from. Every DB reject number was folding our own deliberate refusals in with venue rejections. ROUND 1 BLOCKED, AND THE SURVIVING MUTANT WAS THE THESIS OF THE PR. Against the first head a8c03dcf, mutating the unknown-origin fallback from could_not_tell to broker_reject left 100 PASSED. That single line is the whole point -- 'when we do not know who refused, do not blame the broker' -- and nothing pinned it. ⭐ THE SHAPE IS WORTH RECORDING: codex's three mutants and my own M2 all traversed paths with a KNOWN origin; only the UNKNOWN path was unguarded, and unknown is the case that matters. A guard tested only on its known inputs is untested where it earns its keep. ROUND 2 CLOSES IT, VERIFIED BY EXECUTION AGAINST A 104-TEST BASELINE. M1 replay, unknown -> broker_reject: 1 failed, killed by test_report_origin_fallback_never_blames_the_broker[future_unrecognised_origin-could_not_tell]. M3, which I invented AFTER the correction so it could not have been written to, unknown -> client_abort (the other wrong definite value): 1 failed, same test. M4, deleting the fail-loud closed-vocabulary guard so an unsupported origin is silently accepted: 1 failed, killed by test_refusal_origin_is_a_closed_vocabulary. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 685dc22cdb1ca0b3 with a clean tree. THE CORRECTION IS TESTS-ONLY AND I PROVED IT: git diff between the reviewed head and the new head touches 0 files under src/ -- 34 test lines added, source byte-identical -- so every structural finding from round 1 carries without re-derivation. BEHAVIOUR PRESERVATION IS SEPARATELY PINNED: dropping the accepted->submitted mapping in mark_intent_from_report fails 4 tests in test_oms_risk_service.py, so 'refusal behaviour is unchanged' is a defended claim rather than an assertion. status='rejected' stays stable for existing consumers; the distinction goes in the durable payload. NO MIGRATION AND NO BACKFILL, which is correct: historical rows have no reason and absence remains COULD_NOT_TELL by design. The 08-28 grading is honest and I reproduced it independently from the logs before codex reported it -- 0/22 historically attributable; WHLR client_abort/ASK_PAST_CROSS_CAP; QNRX skipped_before_submit/fanout_webull_collision_managed. ⭐ QNRX IS WHY THE VOCABULARY NEEDS THREE VALUES AND NOT TWO: it was skipped BEFORE any submission and has no fan-out outcome row at all, so a client/broker binary would have forced it into the wrong bucket. NOT MEASURED: I ran two test files, not the full suite -- codex reports 2,947 passed with 14 skipped, taken on report. A wider selection timed out at 85s baseline and I narrowed rather than run it unbounded. ⛔ PROCESS FAILURE OF MINE, recorded because it nearly poisoned a reading: that timeout killed a run MID-MUTANT and my restore never executed, leaving the file mutated in the worktree. I caught it only by hash-verifying the restore. Anything read afterwards would have been against corrupted source. ⛔ DEPLOY: src/** => OMS restart required. Do NOT deploy before Monday's 06:00-06:45 restoration watch reports; #848 is already queued behind that gate and this should follow it, not race it.
